text: The current study evaluated Sonic Augmentation Technology™ (SAT), a novel, Polyvagal-informed probe that incorporates continuously varying and acoustic features modeled on patterns of autonomic regulation into musical soundscapes. Specifically, the study examined whether SAT led to improvements in self-reported biobehavioral state (e.g. relaxation, breathing slowly, interoceptive clarity), and whether individuals with poorer baseline functioning (i.e., increased autonomic reactivity and anxiety/depression symptoms) reported greater improvements in biobehavioral state following SAT. It also sought to determine whether there would be changes in endogenous oxytocin level, and whether individuals who exhibit larger gains in biobehavioral state would show greater increases in oxytocin.
source_label: Feasibility study examining the short-term effects of Sonic Augmentation Technology™
